title: slugify returns the title unchanged instead of a URL-safe slug
goal: slugify(title) turns a title into a string that can be used as part of a URL.

criteria.text: Passing a title to slugify returns a slug that can be put in a URL, so "Hello World" becomes "hello-world".
A space between words is replaced with a hyphen, so "my first post" becomes "my-first-post".
Uppercase letters are lowercased, so "HELLO" becomes "hello".
Punctuation does not appear in the slug, so "hello!" becomes "hello".
Several spaces in a row produce a single hyphen, so "hello   world" becomes "hello-world".
Spaces at the start or end of the title leave no hyphen at the edges of the slug, so " hello " becomes "hello".
Digits are kept in the slug, so "top 10" becomes "top-10".
A title that is already a slug comes back unchanged, so "hello-world" stays "hello-world".

title: slugify returns the title unchanged instead of a URL-ready slug
goal: slugify(title) turns a human-written title into a slug that can be placed in a URL as-is.

criteria.text: Slugifying a title gives back a string that can be put in a URL as-is, so "My First Post" becomes "my-first-post".
A space between words becomes a hyphen, so "my post" becomes "my-post".
Punctuation does not appear in the slug, so "hello, world!" becomes "hello-world".
Several spaces in a row give one hyphen, so "my   post" becomes "my-post".
Spaces at the start or end of the title leave no hyphen at the edges of the slug, so "  hello  " becomes "hello".
Uppercase letters are lowercased, so "HELLO" becomes "hello".
Digits are kept, so "top 10" becomes "top-10".
A title that is already a slug comes back unchanged, so "my-first-post" stays "my-first-post".

title: slugify returns the title unchanged instead of a URL-ready slug
goal: slugify(title) turns a title into a string that can be put in a URL.

criteria.text: slugify returns a slug that can be put in a URL instead of the title as given, so "Hello World" becomes "hello-world".
A space between words is replaced by a hyphen, so "a b" becomes "a-b".
Capital letters are lowercased, so "Hello" becomes "hello".
Punctuation that is not safe in a URL is removed, so "ready?" becomes "ready".

title: parseDuration is an unimplemented stub: it returns null for every input instead of seconds
goal: parseDuration turns a duration string such as "1h30m" into its total number of seconds.

criteria.text: parseDuration turns a combined hours-and-minutes string into its total number of seconds, so parseDuration("1h30m") returns the number 5400.
Each hour in the text counts as 3600 seconds, so parseDuration("2h") returns 7200.
Each minute in the text counts as 60 seconds, so parseDuration("45m") returns 2700.

goal: parseDuration(text) turns a duration string such as "1h30m" into its total number of seconds.

criteria.text: A user can pass a combined hours-and-minutes string and get the total seconds back, so parseDuration("1h30m") returns 5400.
The result is a number rather than a string, so typeof parseDuration("1h30m") is "number".
A string with only hours counts 3600 seconds per hour, so parseDuration("2h") returns 7200.
A string with only minutes counts 60 seconds per minute, so parseDuration("45m") returns 2700.
Text that contains no duration returns null, so parseDuration("abc") returns null.
